stem: Ravi measures his body temperature with a clinical thermometer at home in Chennai. The reading is 37.3 °C. His grandmother says he must be ill because his temperature is not exactly 37.0 °C. What is the correct conclusion?

options.text: Ravi is definitely ill, because every healthy person has a temperature of exactly 37.0 °C.
Ravi's temperature can still be normal, because 37.0 °C is an average and healthy people may read slightly above or below it.
The thermometer must be broken, because no healthy person can have a temperature above 37.0 °C.
Ravi must measure again at noon, because body temperature is only normal in the afternoon.

teacher.key_rationale: 37.0 °C is an average over many healthy people, so a healthy individual can read slightly higher or lower, e.g. 37.3 °C, without being ill. Option B states this correctly; A applies the 'exactly 37.0 °C' misconception, C invents instrument fault, D invents a time-of-day condition.
